root.claim: One deterministic multitape Turing machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed finite number of tapes multiplies two $n$-bit integers exactly in worst-case time $T_A(n)=O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ with $\kappa=2^{-182}$.
root.method: Build two tape procedures that beat one scan per level (an address-chunk interchange and a simultaneous butterfly layer) from fixed linear networks with a strict rank deficit; use them inside the Harvey–van der Hoeven reduction of multiplication to convolution (radix digits, Chinese-remainder axes, Gaussian resampling with chirps, a phase twist to $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$); recover the exact product; and divide every cost by $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$.

motivation.text: The transform calculation consists of address rearrangements, signed shifts and butterflies, and a single scan per transform level already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$; so both data movement and butterfly arithmetic must be done faster than one scan per level.

quote.quote:
Scanning an array of $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of
$\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$.
We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

quote.quote: proposed $n\log n$ as the optimal order of growth

root.salient: The saving is a fixed power of the logarithm, uniform over all input lengths, below the $n\log n$ order that Schönhage and Strassen conjectured optimal, and the address part is obtained for a pure permutation by computing XOR combinations of data.
